content: The management of glucocorticoid-induced hyperglycemia requires careful adjustment of insulin therapy, particularly focusing on basal insulin or mealtime insulin doses. Intermediate-acting glucocorticoids, such as prednisone, typically affect blood glucose levels for approximately 4 to 6 hours following administration. In some cases, patients may need additional doses of rapid-acting insulin or modifications to their basal insulin regimen to adequately counteract the hyperglycemic effects induced by these steroids.
